summary: Keys in about 20 minutes, but any public app using Gmail scopes needs Google verification, and restricted scopes add a security assessment taking several weeks.

approval_wait.label: Several weeks for restricted scopes · exact timeline: not published
approval_wait.notes: Google says restricted-scope verification 'can potentially take several weeks'. A rough, unverified estimate is 14-60 days. Sensitive-only (e.g. gmail.send) verification and CASA assessor timelines are not stated in the pages checked.

prerequisites.notes: Gmail API must be enabled in it.

prerequisites.item: OAuth consent screen / Google Auth platform configured
prerequisites.notes: External user type for general public; Internal limits access to your Google Workspace org.

prerequisites.item: Verified brand info (app name, logo, domains)
prerequisites.notes: Needed for production apps with sensitive or restricted scopes. Privacy policy and authorized-domain specifics were not confirmed.
Required for restricted scopes if you store or transmit the data on a server; repeated at least every 12 months.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: Create or pick a project and enable the Gmail API from the API library.

steps.title: Configure the consent screen and audience
steps.detail: Set app name, support email and user type. Keep publishing status as Testing while developing and add test users.

steps.title: Choose the least-privileged Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Prefer gmail.send or gmail.labels over restricted scopes like gmail.readonly or gmail.modify where the feature allows.

steps.title: Create an OAuth client ID
steps.detail: Create a Web application client, add authorized redirect URIs, and store the client ID and secret server-side.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Use the authorization code flow with offline access if you need refresh tokens. In Testing status, tokens for non-basic scopes expire after seven days.

steps.title: Publish to production and submit for verification
steps.detail: Move the app to In production and submit for verification of branding and sensitive or restricted scopes. Respond to Google's follow-up emails.

steps.title: Complete the security assessment if required
steps.detail: If using restricted scopes and handling data on your servers, complete a CASA assessment with a Google-empanelled assessor, then repeat it at least every 12 months.

scopes.purpose: Send email on the user's behalf.
scopes.notes: Classified sensitive: unverified apps get a warning and a 100 lifetime user cap.

scopes.purpose: Read all email, labels and settings.
Read, compose and modify mail but not permanently delete.
Create and send drafts and messages.
Read headers and labels, not message bodies.

scopes.notes: Restricted. Google recommends it only if you must permanently delete messages.

blockers.issue: Unverified app hits the 100 new-user cap.
blockers.how_to_resolve: The cap applies over the project's lifetime and cannot be reset. Complete verification, or create a new project if the old one was only a test.

blockers.issue: Test-mode refresh tokens expire after seven days.
blockers.how_to_resolve: Re-consent regularly during development, or publish to production (with verification for sensitive and restricted scopes).

blockers.issue: Restricted scope requires a CASA security assessment.
blockers.how_to_resolve: Engage a Google-empanelled assessor, or reduce scopes to gmail.send or gmail.labels. Costs are not stated in the pages checked.
Keep project Owner/Editor accounts and contact emails current so Google's recertification emails are received.

agent_can_do: Recommend the least-privileged Gmail scopes for the feature
Implement the OAuth flow, token storage and refresh handling
Draft scope justifications and the demo-video script for verification
Draft privacy policy content describing Gmail data use and deletion
developer_must_do: Create the Cloud project, consent screen and OAuth client
Own and verify the app domain and brand assets
Submit verification and answer Google's reviewer emails
Pay for and complete the CASA assessment if restricted scopes are used

claims_evidence.claim: Gmail scope sensitivity: gmail.labels is non-sensitive, gmail.send is sensitive, and gmail.readonly, modify, compose, metadata, insert and mail.google.com are restricted.
Apps requesting restricted scopes must complete verification unless an exception applies (personal use, dev/test projects, service-account data, internal Workspace use).
Apps accessing restricted-scope data through a third-party server need a CASA security assessment, re-done at least every 12 months.
Restricted-scope verification 'can potentially take several weeks'; brand verification typically takes 2-3 business days.
In Testing status, test-user authorizations expire after seven days; unverified apps with sensitive or restricted scopes are capped at 100 lifetime new users.
Basic scopes (openid, email, profile) skip the test-user list, unverified warning and 7-day expiry.
Restricted-scope verification is not required for development, testing or staging projects, or for internal use within your own Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization.
A project in Testing status is limited to up to 100 test users listed on the consent screen; test users see an unverified-app warning and their authorizations expire after seven days.

Gmail scopes can be used by up to 100 test users in Testing mode, or by Internal Workspace apps, without verification. Google's docs state the exemptions and the Testing-mode limits on separate pages and do not explicitly equate 'Testing status' with the 'development/testing' exemption; the audience page also says verification applies to In production apps but is silent on Internal apps.
Sensitive-scope (non-restricted) verification does not need a CASA assessment.
Privacy policy URL and authorized domain are required for verification.
Setup of keys takes about 20 minutes.
